campaignDescription: R1 newest-trees-first cold import, second campaign after the memory and drift fixes: pairs P1, P2, S, P3, X and R and the attribution matrix rerun with the fixed R1-U and R1 binaries; P0 reused from the first campaign (r1-newest-trees-cold-20261102, unchanged binaries); on the frozen M4 Mac mini corpus of every admitted Claude Code and Codex source
evidenceIdentity: The binaries were built from commits 3ca7410 (B0), cac534d (R1-E), c36592d (R1-U) and 647a0e5 (R1), before the landed commits' messages were final. The tree is the identity. The landed R1-E and R1-U commits carry trees 3a42c1ff and 839808a7 unchanged. The landed R1 commit's tree is d5c3fa42 (r1-integration 647a0e5) plus this file and the filled R1 measurement sentences in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; neither is compiled.

machine.note: the user's iOS Simulator ran throughout (load1 1.8-3.5 at run starts, 8.6 at the first run right after the release builds; swap flat at about 4,080 MB, grew 0 MB in every run); guard: two consecutive 2 s samples with CPU idle >= 75% before each run; no run proceeded over the guard and none was redone

decisions.U-2: accepted: RootTree ledger frame and rowid order may vary per run; the logical projection must not
decisions.parentR: evidence R's strict section drops surrogate row ids (cursor and message ids), because rebuild numbers cursors in ledger frame order (falls under U-2). Implemented as strict_noid: every cursor id replaced by (runtime_id, path), message ids out. The gate is strict_noid TOTAL; TOTAL_R (without checkpoint file evidence) is reported beside it
decisions.iqrPolicy: every timed pair ran 11 runs per side from the start (P1, P2, S for all three sides, P3), interleaved; P0 is the first campaign's 5+6; X (equalities only) ran 7, and the reported-only P3-stress and E6 rows 5 and 3
decisions.E6StressRow6: --capture-workers N_s at the default look-ahead is the same command at both flag sets; it ran once (E6-default WNS)
decisions.rerun: second campaign (r1-newest-trees-cold-20261102b) after the first one (r1-newest-trees-cold-20261102) failed peak footprint (P2 1.20x, S 1.15x BE-stress) and R1-U's canonical readiness (P1 1.049x). New B1 and B2 carry the fixes; B0 and BE are the first campaign's binaries, byte for byte. P0 (+P0x) is the first campaign's, reused unchanged because neither of its binaries changed. E1.8 structure, stress-prediction.json and N_s are also reused (they depend only on the snapshot and the machine); the predictions were registered against the first campaign's B2

P0: strict equal.likelyCause: cursor ids are SQLite rowids handed out in the order the two runtimes (claude-code, codex) first write their checkpoints; the runtimes race, so which runtime's block starts at id 1 varies. Within each runtime the ids are path rank in every run (strict_local, ids rebased per runtime, is one digest over all runs). No logical, count or provenance difference: only the inter-runtime id offset. This is rowid order, the class U-2 lets vary; the gate is reported as written

P1: CR(B1) / CR(BE).resolved: first campaign: CR(B1)/CR(BE) 1.049 FAILED (drift apply 655 -> 832 ms): T1's order-free drift sample read the offered sample's cursor path and the current sample joined to its cursor on the writer, for each of 185,025 drift events. The writer now keeps each cursor's path and each key's current sample in process RAM (store apply/drift.rs DriftCache, taken out for each writer transaction and dropped on rollback), so only an event that may sort first, or a key's first event, reads its stored sample back. The medians below are this campaign's

P2: peak footprint B2 / B1.resolved: first campaign: peak B2/B1 1.203 FAILED (987 -> 1,187 MB). Two causes, measured with a tagging allocator, vmmap and a C probe: (1) macOS libmalloc keeps the 64 most recently freed blocks over 2 MiB dirty in the footprint, and capture steps free gigabytes of up-to-32 MiB frame and compression buffers; the recency walk and lane S keep the writer busy from the start, so a larger RAM projection coincided with full look-ahead; (2) a running look-ahead step was not counted against the byte bounds, so workers that started steps together overshot them by a batch each, systematically on the big lane. Fixed by rosettad::large_alloc (every block over 2 MiB its own mapping, unmapped on free; macOS only) and by counting a running step's unread payload (at most one batch) against its lane's bounds (pipeline capture/pool). The medians below are this campaign's

P2: newest giant f.likelyCause: structural on this corpus: the newest tree over 64 MiB is 114 h old and holds a single 452 MB transcript. One capture worker reads one source, so that source alone takes about its size / r1_M4 before the tree can close; with CR_ref = CR(BE) that is f of about 0.64. The f <= 0.25 target assumed the newest giant is the newest tree (126 MB, no 452 MB source; brief §12 E1 census, since grown). Splitting one source across workers is §19 (R1.5, streamed pieces). The pre-registered prediction was f 0.673

P2: small-lane 24h@newest and 7d@newest.likelyCause: lane S is writer-bound from the start, not blocked at the sequencer: lane-S writer transactions sit in a standing writer queue (queue wait p50 82.8 ms median over runs; 196.1 ms in the single lane, E6). The 24h@newest small set is the first 4 lane-S trees, 243.0 MB led by the 204 MB live tree of 234 sources; it lands at 0.88-1.13 s in every E6 default row with tree milestones, --experiment-cold-lanes 1 included, so neither lanes nor chunking explain the miss: lane S's own throughput through the writer does. Lanes are what make small-lane 7d@newest work at all (1.61 s against 3.16 s with one lane). Both fractions improved on the first campaign (0.247 and 0.450). The pre-registered f 0.150 and 0.280 are model errors

S: peak footprint.resolved: first campaign: peak 1.146x BE-stress FAILED; the same two causes and fixes as P2's peak

S: small-lane 24h@newest / L1.likelyCause: a tie, not a slowdown: on this corpus the 24h@newest set is small trees only, which the one-lane recency walk also takes first, so lanes cannot beat L1 here and the gate reads as a no-regression bound. The milestone prints at 10 ms resolution and the medians differ by one step; at 0.1 ms (atMs) the ratio is 1.0088, and 1.0024 measured from metadata readiness; neither is a significant difference (Mann-Whitney below). The first campaign's extension pair Sx had 1.008 at 0.1 ms and passed only by rounding (0.915 against 0.91 s). Lane-S service delay is unchanged

S: newest giant f (CR_ref = CR(L1)).likelyCause: the same single-source floor as P2 (the 452 MB transcript in the newest giant is read by one worker); the ratio gate newest giant / L1 passes

R: strict equal without surrogate ids (s.likelyCause: the only differing strict_noid component is ingest_cursor_file_evidence (the checkpoint's $.tail for JSONL and $.snapshot_stamp / $.snapshot_revision for SQLite members): rebuild never stats source files and leaves them null. Task B found the same on B0 3ca7410's rebuild, so it predates R1. Every other strict_noid component, logical and counts are equal (TOTAL_R)
